prompt_context: Draft a Surrender Application before the Magistrate having jurisdiction. CRITICAL — surrender is NOT the same as anticipatory bail. Surrender is the voluntary act of the accused presenting himself to the court to avoid arrest by the police; the prayer is for the court to take cognizance of the surrender and pass an appropriate order — which may be remand to judicial custody OR release on bail (if offence is bailable, or if accused moves bail application simultaneously). Surrender is typically deployed when an FIR has been registered, the accused apprehends arrest, and prefers to be in the custody/under the orders of a judicial forum rather than police. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognised this practice in Niranjan Singh v. Prabhakar (1980) 2 SCC 559 — surrender to court's jurisdiction places the person 'in custody' for the purposes of bail under Section 480 BNSS. The application must clearly state (1) particulars of FIR; (2) genuine apprehension of arrest; (3) act of surrender; (4) prayer for court to take cognizance and pass orders. A separate bail application (regular bail / bailable offence release) is usually filed alongside.
promptInstructions: Draft a Surrender Application — accused voluntarily appearing before the Magistrate to submit to court jurisdiction.
CRITICAL — this is NOT an anticipatory bail application. Do NOT pray for protection from arrest. Pray for the court to take cognizance of surrender.
Open with paragraph identifying applicant and disclosing FIR particulars (number, date, police station, offences).
Set out how the applicant came to know of the FIR (newspaper, social media, friend, police visit).
Establish the apprehension of arrest with concrete facts.
State express surrender to the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble Court.
Include undertaking to cooperate with investigation.
Cite Niranjan Singh v. Prabhakar (1980) 2 SCC 559 on surrender constituting custody for bail purposes under BNSS 480.
Cite BNS sections for the underlying offences (never IPC).
Prayer is for the court to take cognizance of surrender and pass appropriate orders — NOT for protection from arrest.
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
